advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish a present-but-unrecognized `payload['skip']` from an absent one (emit a diagnostic or treat as skipped) so a misspelled/new skip cause is not silently promoted to mutate.
evidence: ticket_planner.py:85 `return tuple(m.payload.get("skip") for m in muts if m.payload.get("skip") in _SKIP_CAUSES)` — the miss path (value present but not in the frozenset) drops silently.
`_classify_early` returns None when `causes` is empty (ticket_planner.py:108-113), so a mutation carrying `skip='tombston'` (typo) is treated as a normal mutate rather than skipped.
ABSENCE: there is no diagnostic or error emitted for a present-but-unrecognized `skip` value, so 'skip requested but unknown cause' is indistinguishable from 'no skip requested'.
advisory.finding: `_skip_causes` silently ignores any `payload['skip']` value not in `_SKIP_CAUSES`: an unrecognized/mistyped skip cause produces no skip classification and the plan falls through to `mutate`, so a requested-but-misspelled skip is invisible rather than an error (fail-open lookup miss).
scenarios: A differ emits skip='partial-snapshot' (hyphen) or a new cause not yet added to _SKIP_CAUSES; the mutation is silently applied instead of skipped

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a `probe` (and `conflict`) mutation on a mutate plan derives zero lifecycle intents.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/ticket_planner.py:118-122 `_intent_kind` returns `IntentKind(mapped) if mapped is not None else None`
test_lifecycle_intent_kinds_derived_from_actions only exercises create/update/delete/repair_property/clean_label — ABSENCE: no probe/conflict mutation is ever planned
Named violating input: `_mk(mutation_mod, "outbound", "probe", "REB-p")` on a mutate plan should yield `intents == ()`
test body: `assert intent.version == obs.version` then `assert intent.version is obs.version or intent.version == obs.version`
The disjunct's `== obs.version` half is reflexively guaranteed given the line above, so the `is`-identity intent of the assertion is never actually enforced
advisory.finding: The newly-added intent-kind derivation maps `probe` and `conflict` actions to no lifecycle intent (`_ACTION_TO_KIND.get` returns None, `_derive_intents` skips them), but no test drives a `probe` or `conflict` mutation on an otherwise-mutate target to assert its `intents` are empty. If the action mapping were widened to accidentally emit an intent for probe/conflict, no test would catch it.
merged_from: In test_intent_version_equals_observation_version_exactly the assertion `assert intent.version is obs.version or intent.version == obs.version` is tautologically true: the immediately preceding line already asserts `intent.version == obs.version`, and the `or intent.version == obs.version` disjunct can never fail once identity is checked, so the second assertion verifies nothing beyond the first.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend test_lifecycle_intent_kinds_derived_from_actions (or add a case) with an outbound `probe` and a `conflict` mutation and assert `by[id].intents == ()` while the plan disposition stays `mutate`.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict `create_targets` (or dependency satisfaction) to creates that actually survive scope/skip/mode/limit/dependency exclusion so an excluded create does not satisfy dependents' requires_create.
evidence: `create_targets` is built from all targets: ticket_planner.py:249-253 `create_targets = { target for target, muts in muts_by_target.items() if any(m.action.value == "create" for m in muts) }`
It is computed before and independent of `limited` (ticket_planner.py:262) and passed unchanged to `_decide_plan`/`_dependency_blocked` (ticket_planner.py:317).
`_is_satisfied` returns True if `prereq in create_targets` regardless of that create's own disposition: ticket_planner.py:131-136.
A create capped by rule 4 gets disposition=defer/safety_aborted but keeps its mutations and stays in create_targets (ticket_planner.py:315-316), so its dependent link is judged satisfied and mutates.
blocking.finding: A create target that is itself excluded (limit-capped, scope-deferred, mode-capped, or dependency-blocked) still appears in `create_targets` and thus satisfies dependents' `requires_create`/`requires_parent` prerequisites, so the dependent plan mutates out-of-order even though the prerequisite create will not occur this pass — violating the create-before-link ordering the change intends.
scenarios: max_changes cap defers the create REB-new (safety_aborted) but REB-link with requires_create=[REB-new] still mutates
REB-new is scope-excluded while a dependent link is in scope
A prerequisite create is itself dependency_blocked (chained prereqs)
blocking.suggested_fix: Compute the set of creates that are actually eligible-and-not-blocked this pass (exclude early-classified, limited, and dependency-blocked create targets) and use that set in _is_satisfied instead of the raw create_targets.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Either drop the currently-unused subset/local_ids scope kinds or define/normalize the id-set key each kind uses so scope exclusion cannot defer every target.
evidence: ticket_planner.py:90-92 keys `subset`/`local_ids` off the same `selection.get("ids")` as `ids`.

The only current selection constructor sets `{"kind": ..., "ids": sorted(...)}` (run_differs.py:291-294), so `subset`/`local_ids` are declared in `_SCOPE_KINDS` but ABSENCE: no caller currently produces them, making the id-key contract for those kinds untested and unspecified.
dropped.finding: `_scope_excluded` reads the scope id set only from `selection['ids']` for all three scope kinds (`ids`, `subset`, `local_ids`); if a `subset`/`local_ids` selection carries its id set under a different key its `ids` is empty and every target is excluded (`target not in set([])` is always True), deferring the entire pass as scope_deferred.
scenarios: A future caller sets selection kind='subset' or 'local_ids' with the id set under a key other than 'ids'
